items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Okay, and I'm Dick Allen. Alright. So, I've got a ton of questions to ask you. Okay, Dick. Sounds great.

ctx.x: When you come back, you visit your family's graves and the shrines and things in our town?

Yes, I do. You see, I have had so many blessings in my life that I made a promise years ago. And this was through my mother and my sister. I don't know what's happened over the last few years. Every time I'd come here, why, she was ready to go with me. Now she doesn't go. But it's one of the promises that I made. I know she'll listen to what I'm saying. That whenever I come here, I would visit the graves of my relatives and pay them the respect that I owe them. Then visit the shrine that my mother introduced me…
You can't reach me through too much. Well, your patron saint is a... St. Jude. Patron saint in lost colleges. Right.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: You said that Dick Allen had asked you to get a few questions for me?

ctx.x: You said that Dick Allen had asked you to get a few questions for me?
Yeah. You said that uh... A few questions and he wanted me to tell you a few things. That's mighty fine. Or maybe you could tell me about Bill Phillips.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Dick Allen still talking to Dono', but the interviewee does not respond with any personal interaction or relationship with Dick Allen, only narrating a story about Earl Hines and George Foster.

ctx.x: Well, we sure in 1974, that's for sure.
Yeah, and Dick Allen still talking to Dono. And we're looking at this letter from William G.
Testing. January 1st, 1974. We're on the second side of this first reel of Don Alba. We're talking about how Earl Hines was a big thing in Chicago coming on with Deep Forest.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher...

ctx.x: I don't know, Dick, but I assume that he is. After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher when Fletcher was on the road. He was always a fickle fellow, wanting a gold, gold, gold, so I imagine he just kept running. And I never heard from him, he's one of the characters that never did Carl Strawn much.
Yeah. But what did he do when the moon changed? Can you tell me?
